title: ACTINA: Adapting Circuit-Switching Techniques for AI Networking Architectures
problem: Static electrical switch networks limit bandwidth allocation flexibility and increase power consumption in large-scale AI systems; dynamic allocation is needed.
motivation: Optical Circuit Switching (OCS) enables dynamic reconfiguration and lower power; but its applicability to AI training depends on reconfiguration latency, bandwidth, and topology design.
method: Framework for evaluating OCS in AI systems; two in-workload reconfiguration strategies; multi-dimensional all-to-all topology supporting hybrid parallelism.
key_novelty: First quantitative framework for OCS in AI networks; demonstrates OCS-enabled multi-dimensional topology achieves 1.75x better perf-power than Fat-Tree/3D-Torus.
contributions: Framework for trade-off analysis of OCS technologies in AI systems
Two in-workload reconfiguration strategies (vs. traditional one-shot approach)
OCS-enabled multi-dimensional all-to-all topology for hybrid parallelism
Up to 2.3x improvement with low reconfiguration latency (<100 us)
limitations: Framework-focused; limited prototype implementation; assumes state-of-the-art GPU bandwidth; reconfiguration latency <100 us is optimistic.
